# Ben Freeborn

> Ben Freeborn works on nutrition and food security for people in displacement settings. He founded From Seed to Shelter, a nonprofit that pilots ways to improve nutrition outcomes for refugees, and currently works with Taimaka on child malnutrition treatment in Gombe State, Nigeria. He welcomes conversations with practitioners, researchers, funders and builders working on refugee food security, malnutrition, humanitarian coordination, and AI for the humanitarian sector.

Ben's aim, in his words: "I want to build a world in which people flee to safety, not more vulnerability."

His work is grounded in first-hand, on-the-ground experience rather than theory alone:

- Six months volunteering in Moria refugee camp, Greece (2020) with Movement on the Ground, plus a further four months in the Greek camps while at university.
- Law degree, University of Oxford; Schwarzman Scholar, Tsinghua University, Beijing. Research on migrant livelihoods in Kenya and Uganda, and ethnographic research on China's Poverty Alleviation Resettlement programme.
- Strategy Associate on People's Courage International's Innovation Team (2024), designing pilot programmes for drought-affected agricultural communities in Indonesia and India.
- Founded From Seed to Shelter (2025) and ran a microgreens pilot at a community centre outside a refugee camp on Samos, Greece. Community members were trained to run the farm, which continues under a local partner, and the results were shared with the World Food Programme.
- From Seed to Shelter is now exploring work in Uganda's refugee settlements, after WFP funding cuts substantially reduced assistance to over a million refugees.
- Collaborates with Ares Intelligence on using AI for humanitarian coordination and on elevating community voices in crisis settings.

## Open to conversations about

- Improving access to healthy, reliable food in refugee camps and settlements
- Reducing child malnutrition (CMAM / outpatient treatment programmes)
- Food security pilots, agriculture and urban farming in humanitarian contexts
- AI tools for humanitarian coordination and community feedback
- Partnerships, funding, research collaboration or pilots in these areas
